title: Pullovers will TRANSFORM your Physique
summary: NH explains why the dumbbell pullover is 'magical': beyond the lats it expands the ribcage by growing the serratus and intercostals, improving the V-taper. He covers execution (across the bench, hips low, controlled depth, elbows tucked, slight bend, inhale on the stretch), fixes for not feeling the lats, rep ranges of 6-15, 1-2 sessions a week, and the need for years of consistency.
claims: Pullovers train the lats, the long head of the triceps and the chest; he considers them one of the best lat builders
The pullover's unique benefit is ribcage expansion: as the weight goes behind the head the ribcage stretches to accommodate it
Before about age 20-22 pullovers may contribute some bone change; after that the expansion comes from growing muscle and tissue
The stretch also trains the serratus, which is rarely trained but important for aesthetics, and the intercostal muscles between the ribs, which can grow and expand the ribcage
Ribcage expansion won't give you a barrel chest; it shapes the area along the ribs into a better V-taper
Never do pullovers lying along the bench: it freezes the shoulder and hips and limits the stretch; lie across the bench with hips low to increase distance between hips and shoulders
Lying across the bench lets you raise the hips as reps get hard to grind out more reps
Going too deep disengages the lats, overloads the shoulder in its weakest range and causes impingement or tendonitis; go deep but not too deep
Think of the ribcage as an accordion: the ribcage, not the shoulder, is what should stretch; return once you reach maximal ribcage stretch
Rotate the elbows inward once the dumbbell is overhead to recruit more lats, limit shoulder flexion and protect the joint
'Reach as far as you can' is a bad cue that overextends the shoulder; keep a slight elbow bend so overextension is impossible
Inhale on the negative to emphasise ribcage expansion, exhale on the way up
Don't bring the dumbbell over the chest for a 'squeeze'; keep it above the head to stay engaged, using the chest position only to rest
If you can't feel your lats, try a barbell for a more neutral shoulder, or bend the elbows a lot like a machine pullover to shorten the lever
Cable pullovers are fine if you feel them better, though dumbbell pullovers are the best
Sensation doesn't equal recruitment; low-sensitivity lifters still grow from pullovers done pain-free
Never go below 6 reps on pullovers because the shoulder joint is what gives out; 6-15 is the range, with slow negatives
Train pullovers 1-2x per week; he does one heavy (100%) and one lighter (~70%) session, the light one to build mind-muscle connection
Beginners at pullovers should start with one session of 3 sets a week and build shoulder mobility and range gradually
Pullovers are great for shoulder mobility, but going too deep too fast gets you hurt
Results take years: Steve Reeves did them for four years, and he saw massive changes two years into doing them twice a week without missing a week
Stick to pullovers for a full year before judging them
exercises: across the bench, hips low and free to rise; slight elbow bend; elbows tucked in; inhale on stretch; stop before overextending; keep dumbbell above head
alternative if dumbbell version not felt in lats
maximal elbow flexion like a machine pullover
shortens lever to better recruit lats
